title: Non-blocking findings from PR #271's review (Daily Homework self-test page)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #271 (frontend-daily-homework-page), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: No `frontend/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` spec was added for the new `/homework` flow (nav to the page, submit the form, see the color-coded score banner) -- the e2e-test skill's own "Relationship to Other Checks" section calls for a new UI flow to get e2e coverage alongside its MSW-mocked component tests. Component tests plus a one-off manual browser walkthrough (both done for this PR's review) cover the behavior today, but the persisted regression suite has no spec that would catch a future unrelated change silently breaking this page.

HomeworkScoreBanner's two "yellow" bands (5-6 "trade cautiously" vs. 9-10 Elder's "too perfect" caution) render with an identical MUI Alert severity="warning" (same icon, same color) and are distinguished only by the body text underneath. Verified in a real browser walkthrough that the text itself is correct and different for each band, but a fast glance that skims past the paragraph could conflate two behaviorally very different messages. Worth reconsidering a secondary visual cue (e.g. a distinct icon, or a small label variant for the high-yellow case) -- a genuinely arguable UX call, not a clear-cut miss, so left as a follow-up rather than blocking.

DailyHomeworkForm.tsx's render gate is `todayQuery.isLoading || suggestionQuery.isLoading`, so the entire 5-question form stays behind a loading spinner until *both* queries settle, not just the one field (`yesterday_trading_score`) the suggestion actually feeds. In production (main.tsx's real QueryClient has `retry: 1`, unlike tests' `retry: false`), a slow/failing suggestion endpoint adds a real, bounded-but-noticeable extra delay before any field renders, larger than the 'sub-second, imperceptible' wait this task's own decisions entry assumed. Consider decoupling the two: render the form as soon as `todayQuery` settles, treating `suggestionQuery` as still-loading (falling back to the neutral default) rather than gating the whole form on it.

When today's entry already exists, `suggestedScore` is never used (the `existingEntry ? scoresFromEntry(existingEntry) : {...}` branch discards it entirely) -- yet the render gate still waits on `suggestionQuery` to settle before showing anything. A user re-opening the page after already recording today's homework waits on a network call whose result is provably irrelevant to what they'll see. Consider skipping the wait on `suggestionQuery` once `todayQuery` resolves with a non-null `entry`.

decisions.decision: Give the 9-10 "too perfect" yellow band a distinct icon (`SelfImprovementIcon`) and a `(too perfect)` label suffix in `HomeworkScoreBanner`, while keeping both yellow bands on the same `severity="warning"` (amber) MUI `Alert` color.
decisions.rationale: The two yellow bands mean genuinely different things (5-6: a middling score, be cautious; 9-10: an over-perfect score, Elder's own caution against overconfidence), and the original review flagged that a fast glance skimming past the body paragraph could conflate them since they render identically otherwise. Considered and rejected: (1) a different `severity`/color (e.g. `info` or a custom palette entry) for the high-yellow case -- this would falsely imply the 9-10 band is somehow less risky or a different category than 5-6, when Elder frames it as its own kind of caution, not a lesser one; keeping both amber preserves 'this is a caution band' as the shared signal. (2) Leaving it text-only as before -- rejected per the review's own finding that body copy alone is too easy to skim past. (3) A generic warning-variant icon (e.g. `PriorityHighIcon`) -- rejected in favor of `SelfImprovementIcon`, which is thematically apt for '(Elder's own) don't let overconfidence change your discipline' rather than an arbitrary second exclamation mark. The label suffix is a low-cost, redundant-with-the-icon cue for anyone not relying on icon recognition (e.g. screen magnification, unfamiliarity with this specific icon).

decisions.decision: DailyHomeworkForm's render gate now waits only on `todayQuery.isLoading`, not `suggestionQuery.isLoading`. `suggestedScore` is read only from `suggestionQuery` once it has settled successfully (`suggestionQuery.isSuccess`), and is never consulted at all in the `existingEntry` (today already recorded) branch. A suggestion that is still pending, has failed, or resolves to `null` all fall back to the neutral default for `yesterday_trading_score` exactly as a failed suggestion already did before this change.
decisions.rationale: This directly implements the two loading-gate follow-up findings: (1) the whole 5-question form no longer waits on the optional suggestion query -- only the one field it feeds can be affected, and only when there's no existing entry to make it moot; (2) when today's entry already exists, `suggestionQuery`'s result is genuinely unused, so the component no longer waits on it at all, confirmed by a new test that never lets that request resolve (`delay('infinite')`) and asserts the banner still renders immediately. Accepted tradeoff, matching the parent task's own established 'no seed-after-mount effect, initial `useState` only' design (see frontend-daily-homework-page's decisions): if the suggestion is still in flight when `HomeworkQuestionsForm` first mounts, `yesterday_trading_score` starts at the neutral default and is *not* retroactively swapped in if the suggestion arrives moments later, since doing so would require exactly the re-seed-after-mount effect that design already rejected (or introduce a remount-via-`key` that could just as easily discard an in-progress edit). This narrows an already-accepted, bounded, non-data-affecting race rather than introducing a new one -- verified with a component test asserting the neutral default renders and is not blocked on when the suggestion endpoint never resolves. Rejected alternatives: keeping the block only for the no-existing-entry case (still needlessly delays the common case of a merely-slow suggestion, contradicting the follow-up's explicit ask); resyncing via a `key` prop tied to the suggestion's settle time (would remount `HomeworkQuestionsForm` and could discard in-progress edits, functionally the same re-seed-after-mount pattern this component's own design already rejects).
